governing_table.code: International Plumbing Code as adopted by Tennessee rule 0780-02-02-.01(1)(d), with no state amendments (the same table is Table 2902.1 of the adopted 2021 International Building Code)
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures
governing_table.quote: The International Plumbing Code (IPC), 2021 edition, published by the International Code Council (ICC).
governing_table.note: The adoption rule was read on the Secretary of State's site (official). The rule lists eight changes to the IBC, none touching Chapter 29 or Chapter 8, and none to the IPC. The table text itself was read on UpCodes' copy of the Tennessee Plumbing Code 2021 and Tennessee Building Code 2021 (secondary): https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ipc-2021/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings and https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ibc-2021/chapter/29/plumbing-systems

cities_may_amend_note.text: Cities and counties that run their own code enforcement ('exempt jurisdictions', which include the large cities) adopt their own editions and amendments. The edition must be within seven years of the newest published one and may not be less stringent than the state's without written approval from the State Fire Marshal's Office. So the city's own table, not the state's, governs in Chattanooga, Knoxville, Memphis and Nashville; the city agent must check each.
cities_may_amend_note.quote: A local jurisdiction that adopts and enforces building construction and fire safety codes pursuant to T.C.A. § 68-120-101(b)(2)(A) shall adopt an edition of a building construction or fire safety code within seven (7) years of the most current published edition. ... no political subdivision of the state of Tennessee shall adopt or enforce any ordinance prescribing less stringent standards of fire prevention, fire protection, or building construction safety than those established in this chapter.

office.row_label: 2 Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: See Section 424.2 (optional substitution, up to 50% of required water closets)
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: See Section 424.2 (optional substitution, up to 67% of required water closets)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts ... 1 per 75 ... 1 per 75

school.urinals: See Section 424.2 (optional substitution, up to 67% of required water closets)

sex_split.text: Half the occupant load is counted as male and half as female, unless approved statistical data show another split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number. In a building with several occupancies, the fractions are added first and then rounded up.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurants) and educational occupancies and up to 50% in all others (offices). The code does not say how to round the percentage; the worked examples round down, since the text says 'not more than'.
urinal_substitution.quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer, in business occupancies of 25 or fewer, or in mercantile occupancies of 100 or fewer.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: IBC Table 1004.5: business areas 150 gross square feet per occupant; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; classroom area 20 net.
occupant_load.quote: Business areas 150 gross ... Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net ... Classroom area 20 net

compartments.text: Each toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door; each urinal needs partitions at least 30 inches apart, starting no more than 12 inches above the floor and reaching at least 60 inches.
compartments.quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 25 / 25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace at most 50% of 1 = 0.5, so 0.
50 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2. Urinals: 50% of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1, total 3. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3, total 5. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25 / 75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0.
100 each. 100 / 75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200 / 75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3. Urinals: 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25 / 50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1. Urinals: 67% of 1 = 0.67, so 0.

hdpe_fire.section: 2021 International Building Code Section 803.9 (as adopted by Tennessee rule 0780-02-02-.01(1)(a) without amendment to Chapter 8), pointing to Section 803.1.1 (NFPA 286 room-corner test)
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1.
supporting_quotes: 803.1.1: Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. (opening words of the sentence partly cut in the copy read: '... materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1.')

Section 202, Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; ...
hdpe_fire.note: Section text read on UpCodes' Tennessee Building Code 2021 (secondary); the state's adoption of the 2021 IBC with no change to Chapter 8 was read on the official rule. Exempt cities enforce their own edition (city agent to check).

access.state_standard: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, named by statute as the minimum specifications under the Tennessee Public Buildings Accessibility Act (T.C.A. § 68-120-204(a)(1), as amended by 2012 Public Chapter 517). The state removes IBC Chapter 11, so ICC A117.1 does not come in through the building code's accessibility chapter.
access.differences_note: None found: the state standard is the federal 2010 ADA Standards themselves, so sections 213 and 604 apply as written. The adopted plumbing code separately asks for 'ICC A117.1' fixtures in shared all-gender rooms (IPC 403.1.1 exception 2); the edition is not stated in the pages read.
access.quote: Any public building that is constructed, enlarged, or substantially altered or repaired after July 1, 2012, shall be designed and constructed pursuant to specifications, approved by the responsible authority, making such building accessible to, and usable by, persons who have a physical disability. The minimum specifications, except as provided in subdivision (a)(2) and Section 68-120-205, shall be the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, and any further amendments, supplements or subsequent editions, or any other code as the state fire marshal determines by rule.

supporting.quote: Remove Chapter 11 Accessibility. ... the provisions of the Tennessee Public Building Accessibility Act, T.C.A. §§ 68-120-201, et seq., shall prevail if such conflict or inconsistency relates to accessibility.

access.process: No separate state accessibility registration or review fee was found. The statute requires the specifications to be 'approved by the responsible authority', and the standard that applies is the one in effect when the project is submitted for final approval. Who the 'responsible authority' is for a given building (State Fire Marshal's Office or the local codes office) is defined in a section not read (T.C.A. § 68-120-203); the official code is on LexisNexis, which could not be opened.

single_user.rule: A single-user toilet room, including a family or assisted-use room, must be identified as available to all persons regardless of sex, and its fixtures count toward the required total. Where only single-user rooms are provided, no rooms designated by sex are required.
single_user.quote: Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed by the state's adopted code. The fixture count is taken on 100% of the occupant load, every toilet must be in its own compartment with a door, and urinals must be visually separated from the rest of the room or each placed in a stall. Not allowed in public colleges and universities, state correctional facilities, juvenile detention facilities and domestic violence shelters (see use_restrictions).
all_gender_shared.quote: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. ... Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.

use_restrictions.rule: (1) Public colleges and universities, state correctional facilities, juvenile detention facilities and domestic violence shelters: since July 1, 2026, each multi-occupancy restroom or changing room must be designated for the exclusive use of females, males or members of the same family, and used only by that sex; single-occupancy restrooms not designated by sex remain allowed (T.C.A. §§ 68-107-101 to -111, 2026 Public Chapter 1052). (2) Public K-12 schools: since July 1, 2021, a school must, where practicable, offer a single-occupancy or employee restroom to anyone who asks in writing for more privacy, and a student, teacher or employee has a right to sue the school if it intentionally allowed a member of the opposite sex into a multi-occupancy restroom designated for their sex while others were present (Tennessee Accommodations for All Children Act, T.C.A. Title 49, Chapter 2, Part 8, 2021 Public Chapter 452). (3) A 2021 law requiring a notice sign at restrooms of businesses that let either sex use any restroom (2021 Public Chapter 453, T.C.A. § 68-120-120) was permanently enjoined by the U.S. District Court on May 17, 2022. No state law was found restricting restroom use in private commercial buildings.
use_restrictions.quote: A public institution of higher education shall designate each multi-occupancy restroom or changing room for the exclusive use of either females, males, or members of the same family. ... This chapter does not prohibit a domestic violence shelter, public institution of higher education, correctional facility, or juvenile detention facility from: (1) Establishing single-occupancy restrooms, changing rooms, or sleeping quarters that are not designated by sex
use_restrictions.quote_schools: A student, teacher, or employee of the public school ... has a private right of action against the LEA or public school, if: (1)(A) The student, teacher, or employee encounters a member of the opposite sex in a multi-occupancy restroom or changing facility located in a public school building; ... and (C) The LEA or public school intentionally allowed a member of the opposite sex to enter the multi-occupancy restroom or changing facility while other persons were present
use_restrictions.quote_sign_law_ruling: On May 17, 2022, the district court issued a permanent injunction striking down the law.

public_wage.law: Tennessee's Prevailing Wage Act (T.C.A. §§ 12-4-401 et seq.) covers state highway construction projects only (streets, highways and bridges). It does not cover schools, city buildings or other building work, so on those only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded work.
public_wage.quote: The Prevailing Wage Act (Title 12-4-401 (Part 4)) protects wage earners from unfair practices regarding pay on state-funded highway construction projects.
public_wage.quote_statute: "State highway construction project" means any construction project for the purpose of building, rebuilding, locating, relocating or repairing any streets, highways or bridges.
public_wage.note: Highway rates are set yearly by the Prevailing Wage Commission (Department of Labor and Workforce Development). Whether any of the four cities has its own wage ordinance for city contracts is for the city agent. The statute copy on tn.gov is dated 2014; a 2026 bill (SB 2229) on highway wage coverage appeared in search results and was not read.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. An out-of-state seller with no physical presence must register and collect Tennessee tax once its sales to Tennessee customers exceed $100,000 in the previous 12 months (retail sales including exempt sales, not sales for resale). If the seller does not collect, the buyer owes use tax at the same rate. Local option tax is added to the 7% state rate (city agent).
shipped_goods.quote: Currently, out-of-state dealers with no physical presence in Tennessee who make $100,000 or more in sales to Tennessee customers must register and collect Tennessee sales and use tax. ... All individuals, as well as businesses operating in the state, must pay use tax when the sales tax was not collected by the seller on otherwise taxable products brought or shipped into Tennessee.

freight.quote: Delivery charges for taxable purchases that are billed by a seller are included as part of the sales price, regardless of the shipping terms and whether the delivery charges are separately itemized on the invoice.
freight.note: Not taxed when a third-party carrier hired by the buyer bills the buyer directly.

install_labor.rule: Labor to install property that becomes part of the real property is not taxed when billed separately on the invoice. Labor to install property that stays personal property after installation is taxed. Whether an item becomes part of the real property (a fixture) depends on the parties' intent and objective factors; the manual does not name toilet partitions.
install_labor.quote: Charges for labor and other services to install tangible personal property that becomes real property upon installation are not subject to sales or use tax if such charges are billed separately on an invoice given to the customer at the time of the sale.
install_labor.quote_2: Installing tangible personal property that remains tangible personal property after installation ... is subject to Tennessee sales tax.

furnish_and_install.rule: A contractor who installs materials that become part of the real property is the user of those materials and pays sales or use tax on their cost. The contract price, labor and markup are not taxed, and the contractor cannot itemize the tax and collect it from the customer. This holds even when the customer is a government or other exempt body.
furnish_and_install.quote: Contractors and subcontractors who improve realty or otherwise use personal property in the performance of a contract are considered the users and consumers of the materials that are used or installed as part of the real property. If sales tax is not paid on the materials when they are purchased, the contractor or subcontractor will owe use tax on the cost of their materials. The construction labor costs of installation or erection and markup on materials are not taxable. The sales or use tax cannot be itemized separately and collected from the contractor's client.

page.stalls_intro: Tennessee's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and every toilet needs a stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, each with a privacy screen. The table shows toilets only.
page.stalls_after: These are the state's minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. Tennessee's larger cities enforce their own edition of the rules, so the city's numbers can differ. An office for 25 people or fewer, or any space for 15 or fewer, may use one shared room.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Tennessee's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Tennessee law uses the federal access standards as its own for public buildings, and the plans are approved by the office that reviews the project.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Tennessee and federal stall rules match:** Tennessee adopted the federal standards word for word, so a stall, door or grab bar that meets one meets the other.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Tennessee's rules a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. Since July 2026, state law requires shared restrooms in public colleges and universities, state prisons, juvenile detention facilities and domestic violence shelters to be designated for females, males or families. A 2021 law covers shared restrooms in public schools.
page.public_jobs: Tennessee's wage law for public work covers state highway projects only, so on a school or city building a set wage applies only where federal money brings in the federal wage rules.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Tennessee, labor to install something that becomes part of the building is not taxed when it is billed separately. A contractor who supplies and installs pays the tax on the materials and builds it into the price, rather than adding it to your invoice.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, freight included when the seller bills it. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Tennessee Department of Revenue

- Toilet counts under the state code: 2021 International Plumbing Code, Table 403.1 and Sections 403.1.1, 403.2, 405.3.4 and 424.2, read on a secondary copy, [Tennessee Plumbing Code 2021, Chapter 4](https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ipc-2021/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings); the same table is [Table 2902.1 of the Tennessee Building Code 2021](https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ibc-2021/chapter/29/plumbing-systems). Floor area per person: [Table 1004.5](https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ibc-2021/chapter/10/means-of-egress). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Fire test for solid plastic partitions: 2021 International Building Code, Sections 803.9 and 803.1.1 (NFPA 286), read on a secondary copy, [Tennessee Building Code 2021, Chapter 8](https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ibc-2021/chapter/8/interior-finishes). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Tennessee's access standard: [2012 Public Chapter 517, amending Tennessee Code Annotated § 68-120-204(a)(1)](https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/acts/107/pub/pc0517.pdf) (Tennessee Public Buildings Accessibility Act), and the [2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design](https://www.access-board.gov/ada/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Single-user and all-gender restrooms: 2021 International Plumbing Code, Sections 403.1.1, 403.1.2 and 403.2, read on a secondary copy, [Tennessee Plumbing Code 2021, Chapter 4](https://up.codes/viewer/tennessee/ipc-2021/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Shared restrooms in public colleges, prisons, juvenile detention and domestic violence shelters: [2026 Public Chapter 1052, Riley Gaines Women's Safety and Protection Act](https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/acts/114/pub/pc1052.pdf) (Tennessee Code Annotated Title 68, Chapter 107, in effect July 1, 2026). Public schools: [2021 Public Chapter 452, Tennessee Accommodations for All Children Act](https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/acts/112/pub/pc0452.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Wages on public jobs: Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development, [Prevailing Wage](https://www.tn.gov/workforce/employees/labor-laws/labor-laws-redirect/wages-breaks/prevailing-wage.html) and the [Prevailing Wage Act for State Highway Construction Projects, Tennessee Code Annotated §§ 12-4-401 to 12-4-415](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/workforce/documents/Contact/PrevailingWageAct2014.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax: Tennessee Department of Revenue, [Sales and Use Tax](https://www.tn.gov/revenue/taxes/sales-and-use-tax.html), [Out-of-State Dealers and Marketplace Facilitators](https://www.tn.gov/revenue/taxes/sales-and-use-tax/out-of-state-dealers-marketplace-facilitators.html) and the [Sales and Use Tax Manual, August 2026](https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/revenue/documents/tax_manuals/august-2026/sales-use-tax-manual.pdf) (delivery charges, installation charges, contractor's use tax). Checked 2026-11-24.

Comp. R. & Regs. 0780-02-02, in force since April 17, 2025; cities with their own enforcement may be on another edition); NFPA 286 for HDPE.

could_not_open: Tennessee Code Annotated on LexisNexis (not attempted beyond the state's link; statutes were read as enrolled public chapters instead)
to_confirm: Each of the four cities is an exempt jurisdiction with its own code edition and amendments: the city agent must check the city's toilet-count table, urinal rule, HDPE fire-test section and single-user sign rule. The state pack applies only where the city has adopted the same 2021 text.

The code tables and sections (IPC Table 403.1, 403.1.1, 403.1.2, 403.2, 405.3.4, 424.2; IBC 803.9, 803.1.1, Table 1004.5, Section 202) were read on UpCodes, not the ICC's own site (403). Browser check on codes.iccsafe.org before launch.
How the 50% and 67% urinal limits round is not stated in the code; examples round down. Confirm with the State Fire Marshal's Office, (615) 741-2241, or city plan review.

Who the 'responsible authority' is for accessibility approval, and the exceptions in T.C.A. § 68-120-204(a)(2) and § 68-120-205, were not read (LexisNexis). Confirm with the State Fire Marshal's Office.

The 2026 restroom act was read as enrolled (Public Chapter 1052); its codified section numbers (68-107-101 to -111) come from the act itself. Whether any court challenge affects it was not checked. The public-school act's codified numbers (T.C.A. §§ 49-2-801 to -805) come from search results, not the act.
A 2025 law on restrooms in 'residential educational programs' was mentioned in a news article and not read.
The status of the 2021 restroom sign law (permanently enjoined May 17, 2022) was read on the ACLU's case page, not the court's order; no appeal is mentioned there.

Whether toilet partitions count as part of the real property once installed (which decides the tax on installation labor) is not stated by the Department of Revenue; it applies a fixture test. Ask the Department of Revenue or an accountant. How Next Partitions itself collects Tennessee tax ($100,000 threshold) is a question for Abe's accountant.
Local option sales tax rates and Tennessee's single-article rules for items over $1,600 were not researched (city agent).
